articles.title: Arizona Wildcats Defeat No. 3 UConn in Close Match
articles.summary: The Arizona Wildcats secured an 85-79 victory against the No. 3 ranked UConn Huskies, despite being shorthanded due to NCAA decisions.
articles.content: Arizona's Wildcats are making a statement in the college basketball world, despite not being at full strength yet. They took on No. 3 UConn and came out swinging, scoring the first 10 points of the game and holding an early lead of 19-5. The Huskies fought back with a furious second-half rally, but Arizona managed to hold off the charge and secure an 85-79 victory. This win has significant implications for the AP Top 25 rankings, as it means that each of the top five teams from the preseason poll will have already taken a loss by December. This is a rare occurrence in college basketball history, with only one other instance of this happening since 2021-22. The Huskies were looking to take over the No. 1 spot in the country if they had won, but now that opportunity has slipped away. Ivan Kharchenkov was a key player for UConn, scoring 20 points and grabbing seven rebounds while making some impressive hustle plays that got the Arizona crowd on their feet. Arizona's bench was severely depleted due to a last-minute decision by the NCAA, which refused to clear RJ Godfrey despite his temporary restraining order in his fight for a fifth year of eligibility. As a result, Arizona played shorthanded against UConn, forcing its top players to log heavy minutes. The Wildcats' Big Four - Kharchenkov, Caleb Holt, Derek Dixon, and Motiejus Krivas - all exceeded 35 minutes on the court, demonstrating their endurance and teamwork. Each of these players rose to the challenge, contributing significantly to Arizona's success. Kharchenkov was a force to be reckoned with, using his strength and agility to overpower opponents and secure crucial rebounds. Meanwhile, Braylon Mullins led UConn with 29 points and six three-pointers, further highlighting the impressive performance of both teams in this closely contested matchup. Arizona point guard JJ Mandaquit made a significant contribution to his team's victory with 11 points, including three crucial three-pointers in just 32 minutes of playtime. This performance was notable considering he had not taken a single three-pointer in Arizona's previous win over Auburn last weekend. It seems that UConn's defensive strategy was to leave Mandaquit largely unguarded at the three-point line. The Wildcats' rotation is surprisingly thin, with only five players who seem to have Lloyd's full trust. This lack of depth could be a concern for the team in future matches. However, there is a silver lining - all five of these trusted players are incredibly talented and capable of competing against top teams. Arizona boasts an elite group of players, with Holt standing out as one of the best on dozens of high-major teams. Dixon's skills would also make him a standout player on numerous other high-major teams. Meanwhile, Kharchenkov's abilities would give almost every high-major team in the sport a run for their money. Krivas is arguably the top center in America. The absence of projected starters from both Arizona and UConn added an interesting dynamic to this matchup. For UConn, Nik Khamenia is currently sidelined due to a broken foot that will keep him out of action for several weeks. In their first road test of the season, UConn's young players initially struggled to cope with the intense pressure. Freshmen like Junior County and Colben Landrew were relatively quiet in the opening half. Na'jai Hines, meanwhile, picked up two quick fouls, which put his team in a difficult position. UConn's supporting cast was largely ineffective for much of the game, forcing them into tough situations. Their attempts to exploit Arizona's drop coverage through Silas Demary Jr. were not enough to make up for their overall struggles. The Huskies' early problems ultimately contributed to their loss in this closely contested matchup. The second half saw UConn's offense transform into a more cohesive unit, narrowing their deficit to just six points in the final minute of play. This resurgence was fueled by Hines' emergence as a dominant force inside, providing much-needed interior scoring. Landrew proved to be a menace on the glass, collecting seven crucial offensive rebounds en route to a double-double performance with 12 points and 10 rebounds. Mullins also excelled, expertly navigating through screens to create open shooting opportunities for himself. Arizona's defense was put to the test, struggling to contain UConn's offense despite the absence of Godfrey on the court. articles.title: Kade Anderson Named Top Contender for American League Rookie of the Year Honors
articles.summary: Kade Anderson, a left-handed pitcher from the Seattle Mariners, is standing out as a top contender for Rookie of the Year honors in the American League after his impressive performance in his first year of play.
articles.content: The Major League Baseball season has come to an end, and the dust is settling on the 2026 campaign. Awards have been handed out, the Arizona Fall League has wrapped up its schedule, and free agents are starting to find new homes. With the conclusion of the season, attention is turning to next year's crop of prospects vying for Rookie of the Year honors in the American League. One name that stands out as a top contender is Kade Anderson, a left-handed pitcher from the Seattle Mariners. Anderson made his professional debut this past season after being selected by the Mariners with the third overall pick in the 2025 draft out of Louisiana State University. In his first year of play, he dominated Double-A pitching, earning a call-up to the majors towards the end of the season. In his limited time in the big leagues, Anderson made an immediate impact, posting a sub-4 ERA in seven starts and striking out 32 batters. His impressive performance in the minors carried over into the show, where he was able to hold his own against seasoned veterans. Anderson's ability to adapt to higher levels of competition has generated significant buzz around his potential for future success. As the Rookie of the Year favorite in the American League for 2027, all eyes will be on him as he looks to build upon this impressive start to his professional career. Anderson's big league debut is set to take place on Saturday as he joins the Mariners' roster. This move comes after a standout season in 2026, where Anderson earned the Pitching Prospect of the Year award. The trade for Luis Castillo and Bryce Miller has opened up opportunities for the southpaw in the rotation. Anderson will face stiff competition from other talented pitchers vying for Rookie of the Year honors. Caden Bodine, a catcher with the Tampa Bay Rays, is another contender for the award despite being considered a middle-of-the-pack candidate. Bodine's impressive 2026 campaign saw him hit 17 home runs and put up strong numbers at both his draft stop and subsequent stops in the minor leagues. Caden Bodine's impressive performance behind the plate has not gone unnoticed. His gold-glove-level defense has been a key factor in his success this season. While offense is also a significant aspect of his game, it's his defensive prowess that sets him apart from other prospects. Bodine's mix of strong defense and offense makes him an attractive candidate for American League Rookie of the Year. However, he may face challenges in terms of playing time. The Rays' recent trade away of their backup catcher could limit Bodine's opportunities to play at the big-league level. This development raises questions about Bodine's chances of winning the AL Rookie of the Year award. The award is not just about a player's ability, but also about their opportunity to play in the major leagues. Bodine may need to prove himself further in Triple-A before he can be considered a top contender for the award. Leo De Vries, an infielder with the Athletics, has been making waves as a potential dark horse candidate for Rookie of the Year. De Vries's impressive start last season caught many insiders off guard, and some had even tipped him to win the award in 2027. De Vries's return to action has been hindered by a shoulder injury that forced him out of commission last season. His status as a top prospect on baseball's Top 100 list makes his current situation even more precarious. For switch-hitters like De Vries, recovery from shoulder injuries can be particularly challenging due to the added strain on their throwing arm. This setback raises additional questions about his defensive versatility and future position on the field. The prospect of an eight-month recovery period means that De Vries won't be able to take the field in a minor league game until at least April. At the major league level, there are concerns about where he will fit into the Athletics' infield lineup. With their shortstop secured for the long term and second base manned by Jeff McNeil, finding playing time on the A's infield may prove difficult for De Vries. The Oakland Athletics' infield is expected to have a new dynamic player in 2027, as top prospect De Vries prepares for his age-20 season. De Vries boasts an impressive combination of skills, including power potential at the plate and exceptional base running abilities, which will allow him to make significant contributions on both offense and defense. His switch-hitting ability also adds versatility to his game. With a strong approach and impressive BB/K rates, De Vries is well-equipped to excel in the big leagues. The rookie's chances of winning Rookie of the Year are still within reach if he makes it to the major leagues in 2027, despite the competition from other talented players in the American League. articles.title: Nick Bosa Still Searching for Dominant Form After Injuries
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa is still struggling to regain his top form this season, despite playing in four games and recording no sacks.
articles.content: San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa is still searching for his dominant form after missing significant playing time last season due to injuries. Bosa's surgeon, Dr. Neal ElAttrache, had predicted a remarkable recovery from the complex knee injury that sidelined him in 2021, saying "with the magnitude of the injury, I can't say that anybody has been better than Nick" after Bosa returned with six sacks and two forced fumbles in seven games. However, this season's stats are less impressive, with no sacks and only two quarterback hits in four games, despite playing 109 pass-rush snaps. Bosa himself acknowledged he is still struggling to regain his top form, saying "I'm going to get better. Kyle Shanahan, the San Francisco 49ers head coach, weighed in on Bosa's performance just days ago, offering a candid assessment that has yet to be revealed publicly. Nick Bosa's performance this season has been a subject of discussion among 49ers fans and experts alike. The key to his inconsistent play may lie in his approach to the game. In a candid admission, Bosa revealed that he had taken for granted certain aspects of his game. This complacency was particularly evident when it came to fundamentals. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, Bosa said, highlighting the issue at hand. He acknowledged that he had assumed he could coast on autopilot and focus on other areas of improvement. However, with a newer defense in place, Bosa recognizes the need to refine his skills once more. The challenges posed by this new defense have forced him to re-evaluate his approach. I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am," he emphasized. Bosa's comeback from injury has been marked by differences from his previous recovery process. He is now 29 and in his eighth season, which may impact his ability to regain his pre-injury form quickly. Furthermore, he tore the same ACL in his right knee last year that he injured as a senior in high school in 2015. The timeline for Bosa's second ACL repair suggests that he may not recapture his full strength until after the 2026 season. This prognosis is based on the typical recovery period of 12 to 18 months, which would put him well into the next season before he can regain his peak performance. Nick Bosa's performance has been under scrutiny due to his four-game stretch without a sack, marking his longest in-season drought. His ability to maintain focus despite the pressure is evident in his approach to handling stress. In fact, he has taken steps to manage anxiety by seeking support from the team's psychologist and limiting his social media use. Bosa's perspective on being defined by statistics as a high-priced pass rusher has evolved over time. He no longer lets stat aspects dictate his emotions, instead choosing to focus on those around him. The stress of slow starts is not new to Bosa; he revealed in the past that it used to consume him. However, now he says his focus is on playing good football and letting the stats take care of themselves. The San Francisco 49ers are facing a challenging time with several key players injured and unable to practice. Cornerback Renardo Green was limited due to a back issue, while quarterback Mac Jones was held out of action because of an illness. Several other players were also restricted in their participation, including Upton Stout, who is dealing with both shoulder and neck problems, as well as Ji'Ayir Brown, who has an ankle injury. Luke Gifford's chest issue also kept him from fully engaging in practice, while Khalid Kareem was limited by his own ankle problem. Meanwhile, rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling continued to work on his recovery from a September ankle surgery and is expected to return to full action in December. articles.title: Sonideros Bring Music and Faith Together at Mexico's Basilica de Guadalupe
articles.summary: Thousands of pilgrims make their way to the country's most important basilica, carrying statues of the Virgin of Guadalupe.
articles.content: Mexico's vibrant streets have become the backdrop for an extraordinary fusion of faith and music as thousands of pilgrims make their way to the country's most important basilica. The annual procession known as the "sonidero" pilgrimage has transformed into a lively street party, attracting devotees from all over Mexico who carry statues of the Virgin of Guadalupe. This significant event is deeply ingrained in Mexico City's daily life, with pilgrims converging on the city's main avenue every year. What sets this procession apart is not just its massive scale, but also the unique presence of street DJs known as sonideros. These DJs are a staple in working-class neighborhoods across Mexico and Colombia, blending cumbia tunes with radio announcements to create an infectious rhythm. Their music has become synonymous with Mexican culture, with sonidero culture being officially recognized by the city government in 2023 as intangible cultural heritage. This designation was met with enthusiasm from UNESCO, which celebrates such unique traditions worldwide. The sonideros' influence extends beyond just their music, they have even given rise to a distinct dance style that is more energetic and open, perfect for street parties, compared to the traditional cumbia. The Basilica de Guadalupe is a revered site in Mexico, attracting millions of devotees each year. Among them are sonideros, mobile DJs who set up shop on the avenue leading to the basilica. Their parties are a staple of the annual celebration, which has been taking place for decades. Faith and music blend together in this unique tradition, with many viewing it as an opportunity to express devotion through joy and celebration. Christian Castañeda, a musician among the throngs marching through the basilica gates, emphasized the significance of the Virgin of Guadalupe in Mexican faith. He believes that by mixing party and worship, they are able to honor their patron saint. Mexicans overwhelmingly identify as Catholic, with nearly 80% of the population holding this affiliation according to census data. This strong religious identity is reflected in the annual pilgrimage to the capital. People travel from distant regions like northern Baja California to express gratitude for good fortune throughout the year. As one devotee prepared for the march, Esperanza Rivera was already hard at work by 4 a.m. She packed sandwiches and put the finishing touches on her family's elaborate pink altar, which would be carried through the streets alongside other festive displays. The sonidero tradition has become an integral part of the annual pilgrimage for many families in Mexico, allowing them to pass down their cultural heritage to younger generations. She urged all sonideros to unite on this special day, emphasizing the importance of coming together as a community. Mobile DJ booths and elaborate flower-lined altars like hers were transported through the streets on motorcycles alongside other festive displays. The pilgrims walked for hours before joining a mass in the Basilica, after which they returned by bus with their fellow sonideros to the Tláhuac neighborhood on the outskirts of the city. This annual event has become a time for families and communities to connect with one another and celebrate their shared traditions. articles.title: Study Reveals Significant Benefits of Arts Education for Students with Disabilities
articles.summary: A new University of Missouri study has found that arts education can improve attendance rates, disciplinary issues, and writing skills in students with disabilities.
articles.content: A groundbreaking new study from the University of Missouri has revealed the significant benefits of arts education for students with disabilities. Researchers followed 2,000 kindergarten through eighth-grade students with disabilities in schools that had expanded their arts programs and found a marked improvement in attendance rates, disciplinary issues, and writing skills. The study, which is one of the largest of its kind, also highlighted the positive impact on students with specific learning disabilities and autism, although further research is needed to fully understand these effects. Arts education can be a vital tool for helping students with disabilities succeed academically without compromising their progress in traditional subjects. The study centered on Houston's Arts Access Initiative, which brought a range of artistic activities to elementary and middle schools. This included artist residencies, workshops, performances, field trips, and after-school programs designed to engage students in creative pursuits. Researchers were able to assess the impact of expanded arts education on students with disabilities because participating schools were randomly assigned to receive enhanced arts programming or not. By comparing outcomes between these groups, researchers could identify any significant differences in student performance and behavior. The study's findings align with long-held assumptions about the benefits of arts education for students with disabilities, according to co-author Kisida. For decades, many educators have believed that the arts are especially important for students with disabilities to succeed, he noted. This is because arts programs often provide alternative ways for students who struggle with communication or engagement to participate and learn. While the study sheds light on the potential benefits of arts education for students with disabilities, it also highlights the need for further research into which specific artistic activities are most effective in achieving these outcomes. The study suggests that arts education can be a crucial component of a well-rounded education for students with disabilities. Arts programs offer more than just an elective or extracurricular activity; they provide opportunities for students to develop essential skills and thrive academically and personally. By expanding access to the arts, educators can give more students the chance to succeed and reach their full potential. Co-author Daniel Bowen is a professor at Texas A&M University. The study's findings highlight the importance of incorporating arts education into school curricula, particularly for students with disabilities who may face unique challenges in traditional academic settings. articles.title: Climate Change Increases Risk of Bat-Borne Diseases Spreading to Humans
articles.summary: A new study warns that climate change and habitat loss could increase the risk of bat-borne diseases spreading to humans, highlighting the potential for natural ecosystems to be disrupted.
articles.content: Bats are known to carry some of the world's most deadly viruses, but a new study warns that climate change and habitat loss could increase the risk of these diseases spreading to humans. A team of researchers from Adelaide University has conducted an international review of bat-borne diseases, including Ebola, Marburg, Nipah, Hendra, and Australian bat lyssavirus. The study was published in the journal The BMJ, where it highlights the potential for these diseases to spread as natural ecosystems are disrupted. The researchers point out that rising temperatures, deforestation, and biodiversity loss are having a significant impact on bat habitats and behavior. As a result, bats are being forced to live in closer proximity to humans and domestic animals, increasing the opportunities for contact between species. A recent mass mortality of flying foxes in Australia's eastern states has been attributed to starvation and weather conditions associated with habitat loss and climate change. The study suggests that this is not an isolated incident, but rather a symptom of a larger problem. The pressures of climate change and habitat loss are having a profound impact on bat populations worldwide. As natural habitats shrink, bats are being forced to adapt to new environments, which could lead to increased interactions between humans and these flying mammals. Bats play a vital role in maintaining the health of ecosystems, serving as pollinators, seed dispersers, and insectivores that help control mosquito and agricultural pest populations. This underscores the importance of protecting bat habitats and preserving their ecological contributions. Protecting bats is crucial because changes to their environments could ultimately have serious consequences for human health. The irony lies in the fact that efforts to safeguard these ecosystems are being undermined by human activities. Reducing the risk of future outbreaks will require a multi-faceted approach, including habitat restoration, minimizing human contact with infected animals, and developing more effective vaccines and treatments. Cities are not immune to habitat destruction, as trees are being cleared to make way for urban development, posing a threat to biodiversity. The loss of mature trees in Adelaide is particularly concerning, as these natural habitats play a crucial role in safeguarding the city's ecosystem and reducing the risk of emerging infectious diseases. When human activities such as agriculture encroach on natural habitats, bats can come into closer contact with livestock, creating opportunities for viruses to spread between species. The Hendra virus in Australia and Nipah virus in parts of Asia serve as examples of how viruses can jump from bats to other animals and eventually to humans. As Australia prepares for another scorching summer, experts are sounding the alarm about the potential for deadly bat-borne diseases to spread among humans. Rising temperatures put immense pressure on bats, which can lead to an increase in the amount of virus they release into their environment, according to Associate Professor Wayne Boardman from Adelaide University's School of Animal and Veterinary Sciences. He warns that this could have devastating consequences for human health. Heat waves not only stress out bats but also make them more susceptible to heat exhaustion, increasing the likelihood of people coming into contact with infected animals. This is a major concern, as it can lead to the transmission of diseases from bats to humans. A creative solution has been implemented in Adelaide, where a large sprinkler system has been installed near the city's flying fox colony to keep bats cool during heat waves. The system, situated 15 meters above ground level in the tree canopy, is designed to protect both wildlife and human health by reducing the risk of contact between people and infected animals. To combat bat-borne diseases, it is essential to prioritize environmental conservation. This involves safeguarding the habitats that bats rely on for survival. By restoring natural environments and reducing human impact, we can minimize the likelihood of bats being forced into close proximity with humans. articles.title: Elon Musk Shifts Stance on Political Affiliations Amid Scrutiny
articles.summary: Elon Musk appeared to take a more measured stance on his political affiliations during an interview in China, distancing himself from Republican Party policies and the MAGA agenda.
articles.content: Elon Musk appeared to take a more measured stance on his political affiliations during an interview in China on Wednesday, where he was part of President Donald Trump's delegation at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The tech mogul made it clear that he does not adhere blindly to Republican Party policies or the MAGA agenda. This shift in tone comes as Musk's business dealings and investments have been closely scrutinized by politicians and commentators alike. Musk has been a significant contributor to Republican campaigns, donating nearly $500 million to support candidates ahead of the midterm elections. His financial backing extended to several Trump allies, including Senate candidate Ken Paxton and Governor Greg Abbott in Texas. The latter two candidates ultimately lost their bids for office, but another Democrat, Gina Hinojosa, who won a seat in the Texas House of Representatives as an -elect, is expected to be a more moderate leader. Musk's Republican push ultimately fell short of its goal to secure a majority with 51 seats by 2029, a target he had set for himself. His significant financial investments in the party did not yield the desired results, leaving him feeling "pretty foolish" about his spending. The outcome was a stark contrast to his earlier efforts, where Musk's generous campaign donations had backfired spectacularly - a $20 million infusion into Wisconsin's state Supreme Court race and $1 million checks for voters in support of a conservative candidate both ended in defeat. In a stark reversal of fortunes, Elon Musk's efforts to curry favor with the Trump administration have backfired spectacularly in his home state of Texas. Criticism is mounting against Musk, with State Sen. articles.title: Preserved Log Houses in Norway Contain Toxic Chemicals
articles.summary: Research has raised questions about the heritage preservation project in Norway due to hazardous substances left behind from conservation processes.
articles.content: Visitors to Norway's open-air museums can step back into the country's past, surrounded by preserved log-built timber houses and farm complexes set amidst historic landscapes. The notion of preserving old buildings has been a long-held one, with these structures being considered irreplaceable cultural assets. However, there is an uncomfortable side effect: many of these preserved homes harbor unpleasant odors, often due to toxic chemicals used in their restoration. According to Anne-Sofie Hjemdahl, a cultural historian at the University of Oslo, research has raised questions about the entire heritage preservation project. This is because Norway's cultural legacy includes an unwanted industrial byproduct: hazardous substances left behind from the conservation process. Cultural historians have recently begun to acknowledge that toxic chemicals were used in large quantities when restoring old buildings throughout the 20th century. The full extent of this problem remains unclear, and experts are unsure how to proceed with preserving these sites without causing harm. Hjemdahl has been working closely with Terje Planke, senior curator at the Norwegian Museum of Cultural History in Oslo, who recently led a project to build a traditional crafts center using an old barn as a workshop for demonstrating traditional skills. The old barn, once destined for renovation as a traditional crafts center, has been deemed unfit due to high levels of toxic substances present inside its walls. Measurements revealed alarmingly high concentrations of creosote and other hazardous chemicals, prompting concerns about the safety of those working or spending extended periods in such buildings. According to Planke, who holds a part-time professorship at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), the risks associated with prolonged exposure outweighed any benefits of renovating the old barn. A new building was subsequently constructed for the crafts center project, leaving the original barn unused except as storage space. This decision highlights the challenge faced by many countries in balancing preservation efforts with public health concerns, especially when it comes to older buildings that may harbor hidden dangers. The discovery of hazardous chemicals in nine Norwegian buildings, including Urnes Stave Church, has sparked a wider discussion about the need for more thorough assessments and potentially costly renovations or demolitions. The debate over preserving historical buildings has taken a new turn in Norway following the discovery of hazardous chemicals in several structures. According to experts, many of these ancient buildings harbor hidden dangers, including flammable and toxic substances that pose significant health risks to occupants. The notion of preserving cultural heritage as it stands is being reevaluated in light of these findings, with some arguing that this approach can be naive and overlooks the potential costs and consequences. It's an optimistic and noble idea, but it comes with certain costs, notes a researcher, highlighting the tension between preserving historical buildings and ensuring public safety. The presence of wood-eating beetles, listed as threatened in Norway, adds another layer to this complex issue, raising questions about whose right it is to protect cultural heritage. The consequences of banning toxic substances from old buildings are now being reevaluated as part of a broader discussion on preservation and conservation. This shift in perspective is evident in the work of researchers who acknowledge that there was initially little consideration given to these issues when the ban was implemented. "Perhaps we buried our heads in the sand," one researcher notes, "but now we have raised them." This newfound awareness has led to a recognition of the need for more comprehensive testing and protection measures. The approach to preservation is also undergoing a significant overhaul, with a greater emphasis on providing buildings with care that goes beyond mere conservation. This can involve tasks such as installing new gutters, according to one expert. Some museums are already experimenting with alternative methods for managing insect infestations without relying on hazardous chemicals. Instead of using pesticides, they monitor the activity of insects and take steps to mitigate their impact. As part of this evolving discussion, heritage researchers are exploring the concept of "curated decay," which involves allowing buildings to deteriorate in a controlled manner to gain new insights and perspectives. This approach could potentially allow museums to convey more nuanced stories about cultural history by incorporating the sounds and experiences of insects that inhabit old buildings. The preservation of cultural heritage has led to a surge in interest for traditional craft knowledge over the past two decades. This renewed focus comes from both the Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Norway's museums. Hjemdahl emphasizes that understanding traditional building methods is crucial, equating it to preserving history rather than merely attempting to halt its progression. articles.title: Knee osteoarthritis affects over 500 million people worldwide
articles.summary: A recent review of four randomized controlled trials found little or no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis when taking turmeric supplements.
articles.content: Knee osteoarthritis affects over 500 million people worldwide, causing damage to cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, leading to pain, stiffness, and inflammation. The condition is often treated with painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs, which can provide relief from symptoms. However, many individuals do not experience significant benefits from these conventional treatments. Researchers have been exploring alternative therapies, including turmeric supplements, which contain curcumin, a compound believed to possess anti-inflammatory properties. Turmeric capsules are commonly marketed as remedies for joint problems, but the evidence supporting their effectiveness is limited and often based on flawed studies. One expert notes that people seeking relief from knee osteoarthritis symptoms may be disappointed by the lack of benefit provided by these supplements. A recent review of four randomized controlled trials compared the effects of turmeric supplements to placebo pills. The assessment aimed to provide a comprehensive evaluation of the evidence, but it found little or no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis. This conclusion may be disappointing for individuals who have tried turmeric supplements in an effort to alleviate their symptoms. Some experts caution that prior studies on the topic were flawed, which may have contributed to the widespread perception of turmeric's benefits. One expert suggests that people should approach alternative therapies with a critical eye and not rely solely on anecdotal evidence or unproven claims. The search for effective treatments for knee osteoarthritis continues, but it appears that turmeric supplements are not a viable solution. More than 370 individuals suffering from knee osteoarthritis were involved in four randomised controlled trials analysed by Shirinsky and his team. Participants were assigned to take either a supplement containing turmeric extract or placebo pills, at varying frequencies of two or three times per day, for periods ranging from eight weeks to three months. The duration of the treatment varied across the different trials. Each trial used a unique supplement with its own curcumin dose. The results showed that participants experienced an average improvement of 6 points on a pain scale, but this was not enough to be considered meaningful according to prior studies. In fact, the difference between the turmeric and placebo groups was half what would be expected to have a noticeable impact. Surveys conducted as part of the study found no significant effect from taking turmeric supplements on participants' quality of life or their ability to perform everyday activities such as walking, standing up from a chair, or climbing stairs. The study's findings suggest that taking turmeric supplements may not provide significant benefits for individuals suffering from knee osteoarthritis. Despite this conclusion, researchers acknowledge that the evidence is not conclusive and cannot be considered definitive. The varying formulations of turmeric used in included studies reduced the certainty of the results. A key issue with the existing research is its inability to establish a clear link between curcumin supplements and their potential side effects. Previous studies have shown that these supplements can cause liver problems in some individuals, but more robust trials are needed to confirm this association. However, experts question whether further research is justified given the current state of knowledge. Experts argue that there is insufficient evidence to support additional trials on the effectiveness and safety of curcumin supplements for knee osteoarthritis. One reason cited is the limited absorption of curcumin into the bloodstream following ingestion, making it unlikely to have a beneficial effect on joints. articles.title: Ground motion model developed for lunar surface predicts higher ground motions at large distances
articles.summary: The new model is specifically tailored for shallow moonquakes and will be crucial for civil engineers planning to construct buildings on the moon.
articles.content: A groundbreaking new model has been developed to predict ground motion from moonquakes and guide seismic hazard assessments on the lunar surface. The model, created by Tessa Williams and her colleagues at Slate Geotechnical Consultants Inc., is specifically tailored for shallow moonquakes and will be crucial for civil engineers planning to construct buildings on the moon in the future. Until now, models developed for Earth have been used to assess seismic hazards on the moon, but these may not accurately account for the unique characteristics of the lunar landscape. The new model predicts significantly higher ground motions at large distances compared to terrestrial ground motion models, which could have significant implications for construction projects on the moon. According to Williams, a distance of 200 kilometers would be considered short to moderate in terms of lunar shaking, whereas it is typically a few hundred kilometers on Earth before shaking attenuates. On Earth, ground motion from earthquakes tends to diminish rapidly with increasing distance, but the lunar surface behaves differently. The new model takes into account these unique properties and shows that strong shaking can persist even at distances over 1,000 kilometers for small-magnitude events. This has significant implications for construction projects on the moon, where buildings must be designed to withstand such extreme seismic activity. The development of a lunar-specific ground motion model is a major breakthrough in preparing for human exploration and potential settlement of the moon. As Williams notes, terrestrial models are not sufficient for predicting ground motions on the moon due to its unique geology and gravitational properties. The moon's unique geology and gravitational properties make it challenging for scientists to predict ground motions on its surface. To aid structural engineers designing new lunar structures, researchers evaluated the impact of lunar seismicity. They reviewed data from the Apollo missions, which revealed significant differences between lunar and Earth seismicity. Seismic waves propagate through the moon in ways that are distinct from those on our planet. Williams noted that terrestrial models would not accurately capture the potential shaking on the moon due to its unique properties. The amplitude of shaking at large distances and the long durations of these events do not resemble earthquakes, making it difficult to apply Earth-based models. The researchers used a combination of historical data from Apollo-era moonquake recordings and physics-based simulations to create a lunar-specific ground motion model. This approach accounted for the moon's distinct geological features that affect seismic wave propagation. The team noted that the lunar interior is colder and more solid than Earth's, resulting in less energy loss as seismic waves pass through. The fractured lunar surface also plays a crucial role in scattering seismic energy, making it essential to consider this factor in models. By incorporating these characteristics into their simulations, Williams and her colleagues were able to produce results that better matched the Apollo seismic recordings. This improvement suggests that their model is more accurate for predicting ground motions on the moon. Lunar recordings have an unusually long duration compared to earthquake recordings, which the researchers' model did not fully capture. Despite this limitation, the team's work represents a significant step forward in understanding and predicting seismic activity on the moon. The researchers found that moonquakes typically last much longer than their Earth-based counterparts, with an average strong-shaking duration of around 54 minutes. This prolonged shaking is likely due to the way seismic energy interacts with the moon's fractured upper crust, causing it to scatter and spread out over a longer period. As a result, the ground motion experienced on the lunar surface can be quite different from what would occur during similar events on Earth. The current dataset of moonquake recordings has some limitations that affect the accuracy of the new ground motion model developed by the team. The data comes from just four closely spaced stations, which captured seismic wave information in a relatively narrow frequency range. A more comprehensive and detailed record of lunar seismic activity would be beneficial for refining the model and ensuring it can accurately predict potential hazards to structures on the moon's surface. articles.title: El Niño Winter Storms Highlight Hidden Threat to Coastal Cities
articles.summary: Rising groundwater poses a significant threat to coastal cities due to its ability to contaminate soil and water sources, leading to health risks and infrastructure damage.
articles.content: Coastal communities are bracing for the impact of El Niño winter storms, but their focus is on the obvious: surging high tides and pounding waves spilling over seawalls. Decades of storm coverage have trained us to measure climate risk by what crashes onto the shoreline. However, this hyperfocus on surface-level threats overlooks a more insidious danger lurking beneath our feet. Researchers at UC Berkeley are uncovering how rising water tables pose a significant threat to coastal cities long before the ocean overtakes the beach. The key factor in this threat is rising groundwater, which can have devastating consequences for urban infrastructure. To better understand and mitigate this risk, researchers are using spatial modeling and hydrological data to map the impact of sea level rise on coastal communities. As environmental planner Kristina Hill explains, the real threat is not just what's happening at the surface, but also what's happening beneath our feet. Coastal cities rely on a layer of fresh groundwater to support their dry crust of land, which floats over dense saltwater pushing from the ocean into the land. However, as ocean levels rise, this subterranean saltwater wedge presses farther inland, forcing the fresh groundwater toward the surface. The pressure from below is what's driving the water upward, making conventional barriers like levees or concrete seawalls eventually ineffective in keeping out the rising water. This means that problems can arise long before surface seawater reaches a city's front door. Hill's research highlights the role of rising groundwater in causing issues such as backing up sewer pipes and corroding building foundations. However, the most concerning effect is the mobilization of buried toxins and soil contaminants, which poses significant risks to public health. Regional water table mapping across coastal environments has been a key component of Hill's research. By analyzing thousands of groundwater measurements, her team has created detailed maps of contaminated zones in areas like the San Francisco Bay Area. The team's findings have far-reaching implications for environmental justice, revealing that low-income neighborhoods and communities of color are disproportionately affected by living near these vulnerable zones. This reframes the issue as an active public health emergency, rather than a distant shoreline concern. Adaptive engineering strategies can help coastal cities cope with rising water levels by embracing rather than fighting against it. Inspiration for these innovative approaches comes from various sources, including ancient floating districts in Mexico City and modern Dutch water management techniques. The incorporation of new water bodies, such as those created through excavation, allows for the construction of floating housing units that can accommodate residents. This type of design is not only environmentally friendly but also provides a safe and sustainable living space. In addition to engineering solutions, Hill's work highlights the importance of combining field monitoring with public engagement in order to develop effective adaptive strategies. By working together with community members, cities can identify areas of high risk and implement targeted measures to protect public health and property values. This approach not only preserves social ties but also helps maintain property values. Ultimately, shifting the conversation from fighting sea level rise to adapting to it empowers coastal communities to innovate and build resilience in a changing climate. articles.content: JPMorgan Chase has appointed Bregje de Best as its next chief financial officer, a move that marks a significant shift within the company's leadership structure. De Best, who joined JPMorgan in 2006 and has spent two decades at the firm, will take over the role of CFO from Jeremy Barnum after he steps down following the first-quarter 2027 financial reporting period. The announcement was made by the company on Tuesday. De Best's appointment as CFO is a significant milestone for the 43-year-old Dutch banker, who currently serves as CFO of JPMorgan's commercial and investment bank (CIB). She has held various senior roles within the firm, including co-head of global corporate banking, and has also worked in investment banking and markets in the UK and Asia. As she prepares to take on her new role, de Best will join the firm-wide operating committee. Jeremy Barnum, who has been CFO for six years, has informed the company that he intends to conclude his tenure as CFO after the first-quarter 2027 financial reporting period. He will then become a vice chairman of JPMorgan Chase, with Bregje de Best succeeding him in the role. De Best's appointment is also notable because she will be the latest woman to serve as JPMorgan's CFO. De Best has been at the forefront of various key initiatives within JPMorgan's commercial and investment bank (CIB) since June 2025, where she currently serves as CFO. Her background in investment banking and markets in the UK and Asia adds significant depth to her experience and expertise. As de Best prepares to take on her new role, the company will be watching closely to see how her leadership style and vision shape the future of JPMorgan Chase's finance organization. JPMorgan's next Chief Financial Officer will have a unique blend of investment banking expertise and operational experience, thanks in part to her tenure as CFO of the bank's Corporate & Investment Bank (CIB) division. De Best's background is not uncommon among current CFOs - 22% of those at companies in the combined Fortune 500 and S&P 500 sample have investment banking experience. Furthermore, of these individuals with an investment banking background, a significant proportion - 20% - work within the financial industry. As CIB CFO, de Best oversees business management and controls across JPMorgan's global banking, markets, payments and securities services businesses. This operational expertise is becoming increasingly valuable in companies seeking to navigate complex financial landscapes. De Best herself has spoken about the rapidly changing nature of the bank's business, citing the impact of AI and digital assets on its operations. In a recent LinkedIn post, she wrote that these trends are driving her commitment to innovation and leadership within the industry. Bregje de Best is set to take on a new role as JPMorgan's Chief Financial Officer, succeeding Tumpel Gillesen. As part of this transition, she will work closely with her predecessor, who will remain at the company until early 2028. During that time, he will oversee key events such as the January and April earnings announcements and the Investor Day in February. As vice chairman following first-quarter reporting, her predecessor will continue to play a significant role in firm-wide initiatives alongside Jamie Dimon and other senior leaders. This continuity choice has been highlighted by analysts, who note that de Best's background at JPMorgan Chase is similar to her predecessor's experience. Both have served as CFO for the commercial and investment bank segment prior to their current roles. The company will announce de Best's successor as CFO of the CIB early next year, ensuring a smooth transition in leadership. articles.title: Quantum Computers Utilize Light Particles for Complex Calculations
articles.summary: Researchers at Paderborn University have been studying the potential of photonics-based quantum computers, which use light particles to perform calculations beyond traditional computer capabilities.
articles.content: Researchers at Paderborn University in Germany have been exploring the potential of photonics-based quantum computers to tackle complex problems that are beyond the capabilities of even the most powerful supercomputers. These devices utilize the unique properties of light particles to perform calculations that would be impossible for traditional computers, opening up new avenues of research in fields like energy and chemical research. The team, led by Dr. Christine Silberhorn, has been using Germany's first scalable photonic quantum computer, a "Gaussian boson sampler, to investigate the fundamental question of which quantum resources are most important for its performance. This device is designed to process and sample complex light patterns, but understanding how individual quantum resources contribute to its capabilities is crucial for optimizing its use. The researchers have published their findings in the journal PRX Quantum, using data obtained from the Paderborn Quantum Sampler (PaQS). The new research builds on previous work demonstrating a large-scale quantum system, and takes a more nuanced approach by examining the individual components that enable the device's capabilities. This investigation is an important step towards developing practical applications for photonics-based quantum computers, which could have significant impacts on various fields of study and industry. As researchers continue to refine their understanding of these devices, we can expect new breakthroughs in areas such as energy research, chemical analysis, and secure communication systems. The development of the photonic quantum computer was made possible by combining expertise in integrated photonics from Paderborn with insights from computer science and theoretical quantum optics. This collaboration led to the creation of a flexibly programmable device based on scalable components, along with new methods for evaluating the role of various quantum resources in its performance. Researchers working within a Germany-wide research collaboration made significant contributions to this project. They not only developed and integrated specialized hardware but also created novel data analysis methods and a theoretical framework for interpreting measurement results. This comprehensive approach is essential for advancing the field of quantum computing. According to Dr. Michael Stefszky, understanding how properties such as squeezed light, photon statistics, and entanglement impact computational performance is crucial for developing the next generation of quantum technologies. The results underscore that building useful quantum computers involves far more than simply scaling up a system," he explains. PaQS, a machine designed to sample Gaussian bosons, measures the points at which photons leave a complex photonic network through which they are guided. This task becomes increasingly difficult for conventional computers as the number of photons increases and the network complexity grows. Determining these patterns can be computationally intensive, with simulations on a supercomputer taking thousands of years for large systems. The development of such devices like PaQS is crucial in advancing our understanding of quantum resources and their role in computational performance. The PaQS system offers a high degree of programmability, allowing researchers to configure its photonic network for various experiments. This flexibility turns the system into an adaptable research platform rather than a single-purpose device. As a result, the team can explore new approaches and potential applications as the field of research continues to evolve. The researchers are currently expanding the system to support more complex calculations and investigate further potential applications for photonic quantum computing. By doing so, they aim to contribute both a high-performance experimental system and new insights into the quantum resources that will shape the performance of future photonic quantum computers. In their work, the Paderborn team is shedding light on the fundamentals governing the performance of photonic quantum computers. articles.title: Land-use Intensity Affects Biodiversity Differently Across Species Groups
articles.summary: Researchers from the University of Göttingen have found that intensive agriculture leads to a significant decline in local species diversity, with monoculture areas averaging around 50% fewer species than rainforests.
articles.content: The conversion of tropical rainforests into large-scale plantations for crops like rubber and oil palms poses a significant threat to global biodiversity. But surprisingly, this process does not always lead to a homogenization of species in these areas. Researchers from the University of Göttingen have been studying how different landscapes along the Indonesian island of Sumatra's tropical lowlands respond to varying levels of land use intensity. Their analysis spanned 32 plots, ranging from untouched forests to traditional rubber farming and intensive smallholder monocultures of either rubber or oil palm. The team discovered that the impact of land-use intensity on biodiversity is far more complex than expected, with different organisms reacting differently to their surroundings. The researchers analyzed data from 40,000 species across 24 different groups to understand how land-use intensity affects biodiversity. Their findings indicate that intensive agriculture leads to a significant decline in local species diversity, with monoculture areas averaging around 50% fewer species than rainforests. At the landscape level, this decline is even more pronounced, reaching as high as 78%. According to Dr. Nathaly Guerrero-Ramírez, the sharp decline in species numbers does not necessarily translate to increased similarity in community composition within monoculture areas. Instead, the data suggests that communities with fewer species still contain subsets of those found in richer ecosystems. The findings of a recent study suggest that focusing solely on species richness is not enough to fully understand the ecological consequences of land use in tropical regions. In order to effectively conserve nature, researchers emphasize that it's crucial to consider entire landscapes rather than individual protected areas or plantations. This involves examining which species occur together in different locations and how their communities are structured. By taking this approach, conservation efforts can be more targeted and effective. The study highlights the importance of understanding habitat diversity and the relationships between different groups of organisms. Only by considering these factors can we hope to limit the loss of tropical biodiversity and preserve the complex ecosystems that exist in these regions. articles.title: Newly Discovered Crab Species Found in South China Sea
articles.summary: A newly discovered crab species from the South China Sea has sparked interest in the evolutionary history of deep-sea creatures.
articles.content: A newly discovered crab species from the South China Sea has sparked interest in the evolutionary history of deep-sea creatures. The crab, known as Macromedaeus putrimanubriatus, was found at depths of approximately 330-980 feet, a vast difference from its closely related cousin M. orientalis which inhabits intertidal zones. Led by Sha Zhongli from the Institute of Oceanology of the Chinese Academy Sciences (IOCAS), a research team has described this new species in the Xanthidae family and published their findings in Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society. The fact that modern deep-sea fauna has traditionally been seen as resulting from ancient colonizations dating back to the middle Paleozoic to early Cenozoic era may not be entirely accurate, new evidence suggests. Macromedaeus species have long been known to inhabit nearshore rocky intertidal zones with broad, flattened carapaces and robust walking legs; however, Macromedaeus putrimanubriatus stands out with its narrower carapace and slender walking legs. Phylogenetic analyses have placed Macromedaeus putrimanubriatus firmly within its genus and confirmed its close relationship to M. orientalis, a species found in intertidal zones. The research highlights the significance of genetic data in understanding the evolutionary history of this group. Studies suggest that M. putrimanubriatus and M. orientalis diverged from their common ancestor approximately 13 million years ago, around the time when the Antarctic ice sheet expanded rapidly and the climate cooled significantly. This period saw a significant drop in sea level and reorganization of ocean circulation patterns. The researchers propose that changes in shallow-water environments or the availability of deep-water niches may have driven the ancestors of M. putrimanubriatus out of their intertidal habitats and into deeper waters. This shift could be linked to variations in food supply or vacant ecological spaces. Comparative studies across other Xanthoidea groups reveal a similar trend: deep-water species tend to possess narrower carapaces and more slender legs, features that are thought to have evolved independently as adaptations to soft bottoms, dispersed resources, and reduced predation pressure. These traits facilitate movement over sediment and minimize energy expenditure. Convergent evolution is evident in the shared morphological traits of deep-water Xanthoidea species, which have developed similar body plans despite their distinct evolutionary paths. This phenomenon underscores the importance of environmental pressures in shaping the physical characteristics of organisms. The discovery of a new crab species in the South China Sea has shed light on the rapid evolution of deep-water organisms. This newly described species is part of a relatively recent colonization event, where shallow-dwelling creatures adapted to life in deeper waters. The study highlights that this shift has led to the formation of younger lineages alongside ancient ones within modern deep-water fauna. Such findings underscore the significant impact of environmental pressures on shaping the physical characteristics of organisms. The researchers chose to name the new species after a Chinese legend, symbolizing how rapidly morphology can diverge under selective pressures in deep-water environments. According to Dr. Yuan Ziming, first author of the study, this choice underscores the remarkable adaptability of deep-sea creatures. These findings provide crucial evidence for understanding the evolution and formation history of deep-sea fauna. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-11-newly-south-china-sea-crab.html
